mainTopic: Examining נגעים on the festival: the כהן's role, רבי's two reported rulings, whether a מוחלט is permitted to his wife, and delaying the examination for a חתן or a רגל
overview: The גמרא explains that a כהן can examine a נגע on the festival 'only to be lenient' when the person is in his second הסגר. There רבי מאיר says the כהן may declare him pure or simply stay silent, while רבי יוסי says the פסוק requires him to announce either result. Two ברייתות report רבי's compromise in opposite ways. The גמרא explains that two תנאים disagree about what matters more to a healed מוחלט: rejoining people, or staying with his wife, since the seven counting days forbid him to her. This leads to a side discussion of whether a מוחלט is permitted to his wife. רבי יהודה and רבי say yes, with a proof from King עוזיהו, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids it by קל וחומר. Finally a ברייתא teaches that the כהן puts off the examination during a חתן's seven feast days and during a רגל. רבי learns this from emptying a house, and אביי and רבא discuss what difference the two sources make.

steps.title: The case is a second week of quarantine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its earlier question about when examining 'to be lenient' is possible: it is during the second הסגר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a person in his second week of quarantine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it asked just before: in what case can a כהן examine a נגע on the festival 'only to be lenient'? The answer is a person already in his second week of הסגר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At earlier examinations the כהן might have a third ruling to give, such as another week of הסגר. At the end of the second הסגר only two results remain: pure or confirmed impure. So the כהן can announce 'pure' if that is the result, or simply stay silent if he is impure. That is why examining him 'for leniency' makes sense here.

keyTerms.meaning: Quarantine: a week of being shut away while the כהן waits to see how the נגע develops
Second
A צרעת mark on the skin

phrases.english: In the second quarantine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the preceding question (on the previous side of the daf) about how examining 'to be lenient' could work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case can a כהן examine a נגע on the festival only for a lenient outcome?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the person is in his second הסגר, where a declaration of purity is possible.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the כהן may stay silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's reasoning: the status depends on the כהן's declaration, so he can declare 'pure' and stay silent if the person is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (רבי מאיר) holds that the matter depends on the כהן. If the person is pure, the כהן tells him 'pure'. If he is impure, the כהן stays silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר allows examining for leniency only. Nobody becomes impure until a כהן says the word 'impure'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the person's status is created by the כהן's words, not only by what the skin looks like. So the כהן can examine him on the festival. If the person is pure, the כהן announces it and the person is happy. If he is impure, the כהן says nothing and the festival is not ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter depends on the כהן: only his declaration sets the status
Pure
Impure
He stays silent

steps.confusionAlert: The כהן's silence does not mean the person is pure. It only means he has not been declared a confirmed מצורע (מוחלט). He stays in his current status as a מוסגר until a כהן speaks.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, who allowed examining for leniency.

phrases.english: The matter depends on the priest.
If he is pure, he says to him, "Pure,"
and if he is impure, he stays silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of רבי מאיר within the case set up in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is impure only when a כהן declares it, so a כהן may examine on the festival and keep silent if he finds impurity.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the כהן must declare either way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's reasoning: the פסוק says 'to purify or to make impure', so the כהן cannot pick only the lenient side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other master (רבי יוסי) holds that it is written, 'to declare him pure or to declare him impure'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי, who does not allow examining at all on the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה puts 'purify' and 'make impure' together in one phrase. So whenever the כהן examines, he must announce whatever he finds. Since he would have to say 'impure' if that is the result, he should not examine during the festival at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To declare him pure or to declare him impure (from the פסוק)
It is written

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the כהן's word decides, so he may stay silent. רבי יוסי: the פסוק requires him to declare either result, so he may not examine on the festival.

phrases.english: And the other master holds: "To pronounce him pure or to pronounce him impure" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning to רבי מאיר's view in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק links purifying and making impure, so a כהן who examines must declare whatever he finds.

steps.title: Re-quoting רבי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי's statement from the ברייתא in order to analyze it: רבי יוסי applies to a מוחלט, רבי מאיר to a מוסגר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said that רבי said: רבי יוסי's words seem right for a confirmed מצורע, and רבי מאיר's words seem right for a quarantined one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-quotes רבי's compromise ruling from the ברייתא. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי splits the case. A confirmed מצורע (מוחלט) should not be examined on the festival, like רבי יוסי. A quarantined person (מוסגר) may be examined for leniency, like רבי מאיר. The גמרא repeats this ruling because it is about to question it.

keyTerms.meaning: Seem correct
A confirmed מצורע, declared definitely impure
A quarantined person, impure for now but not yet confirmed as a מצורע

phrases.english: The master said: Rabbi said:
The words of Rabbi Yosei seem correct regarding a confirmed leper,
and the words of Rabbi Meir regarding a quarantined leper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי dispute to analyzing רבי's ruling on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי rules like רבי יוסי for a מוחלט and like רבי מאיר for a מוסגר.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the quote: a different ברייתא reports רבי as saying the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't the opposite taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that another ברייתא quotes רבי the other way around. In that version, רבי יוסי applies to a מוסגר and רבי מאיר to a מוחלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources report opposite rulings in the name of the same person, רבי. That is a contradiction about what רבי actually held, and the גמרא must resolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, reversed

phrases.english: But isn't the opposite taught!
phrases.notes: Another ברייתא quotes רבי the other way around: רבי יוסי's view for the מוסגר, and רבי מאיר's for the מוחלט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling quoted in step 4 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling as quoted in the ברייתא (step 4)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא attributes the reverse division to רבי, so the two reports contradict each other.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about רבי: being among people
steps.stepSummary: Answer: two תנאים report רבי differently. The one who allows examining a מוחלט holds that rejoining society matters most to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים about what רבי held. One master holds that being back in the company of people is more precious to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying two תנאים disagree about what רבי held. It then explains the first view: the version that allows examining a מוחלט on the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מוחלט is found to be healed, he may leave isolation and return to the community, which brings him great joy. If he is not healed, he is no worse off than before. So, for someone who values rejoining people most, examining him on the festival can only help.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
According to, in the opinion of
Company, companionship
The world, people in general
Is preferable to him

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים according to Rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: צַוְותָּא דְעָלְמָא עֲדִיף לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: One master holds: the company of the world is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that allows examining the מוחלט, since being freed to rejoin people makes him happy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different תנאים reporting רבי's view differently (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to report one single position of רבי, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא reflects a different תנא's understanding of רבי, based on what matters more to the מצורע.

steps.title: The other view: being with his wife
steps.stepSummary: The second תנא holds that being with his wife matters more. So a מוחלט should not be examined, because purification would forbid him to his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other master holds that being with his wife is more precious to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining the other ברייתא, the one quoted first, which forbids examining a מוחלט on the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוחלט who is healed begins a seven-day purification, and during that time he may not be with his wife. For someone who values that more than rejoining people, a 'good' result would actually bring him sadness on the festival. So he should not be examined then, like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife
Being together with his wife

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רבי agree the festival's joy must be protected. They disagree about what brings a healed מוחלט more joy: rejoining society, or staying with his wife, which the seven-day purification would interrupt.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: צַוְותָּא דְאִשְׁתּוֹ עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: the company of his wife is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: A healed מוחלט counts seven days before he is fully pure, and he may not be with his wife then. So examining him would upset him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר: צַוְותָּא דְאִשְׁתּוֹ עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 6 by explaining the opposing תנא's view of רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completes the תנאי היא answer by giving the reasoning behind the first ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא quoted in step 4 holds that being with his wife matters more, so a מוחלט is not examined on the festival.

steps.title: Is a confirmed leper really permitted to his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the previous answer really means that a מוחלט is permitted to be with his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that a confirmed מצורע is allowed to be with his wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check something the last answer assumed. That answer said purifying a מוחלט would forbid him to his wife, which suggests that before purification he is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 explained that the second תנא does not want a מוחלט examined, because once he is purified his counting days forbid him to his wife. That reasoning only works if a מוחלט himself is permitted to his wife. The גמרא asks openly whether that is really the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a question about what follows from a statement)
A confirmed מצורע, declared fully impure by the כהן
Marital relations

phrases.english: Is this to say that a confirmed leper
is permitted in marital relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the hidden assumption behind the answer in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a confirmed מצורע is in fact permitted to be with his wife.

steps.title: Yes: a ברייתא forbids only the counting days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and brings a ברייתא that learns from 'outside his tent' that a מצורע in his seven counting days is forbidden to his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. And so a ברייתא teaches: 'He shall stay outside his tent seven days' means he is forbidden to be with his wife. 'His tent' means his wife, as the פסוק says, 'Go tell them: return to your tents.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'yes' and begins quoting a ברייתא to back this up. This first part shows where the prohibition during the counting days comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a מצורע's seven counting days says he stays 'outside his tent'. The ברייתא reads 'tent' as 'wife', based on the פסוק where the people were told to return to their tents, meaning their wives. So the prohibition is written about the counting days, which sets up רבי יהודה's point in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
His tent, read here as 'his wife'
The seven counting days after a מצורע is healed, before he is fully pure

phrases.english: Yes, and so it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he shall stay outside his tent seven days"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:8. This is about a מצורע who has been healed and is counting his seven days.

phrases.english: meaning that he is forbidden in marital relations.
And "his tent" means nothing other than his wife,
as it says: "Go say to them:
Return to your tents."
phrases.notes: דברים 5:27. After מתן תורה the men were told to go back to their wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with 'yes' and starts bringing a supporting ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, a מוחלט is permitted; the ברייתא locates the prohibition in the counting days.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: counting days forbidden, confirmed days not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה in the ברייתא says the prohibition applies to the days of counting and not to the days of being a confirmed מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'Seven days they shall count for him' teaches that the prohibition is during his counting days, not during his confirmed days.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part of the ברייתא that actually proves the 'yes'. רבי יהודה says outright that a confirmed מצורע is not forbidden to his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ties the prohibition to the 'counting' days specifically. Since the Torah wrote it only about the counting days, the days of being confirmed are left out. This matches the assumption in step 7 that a מוחלט is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall count for him
The days when he is a confirmed מצורע

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards: the confirmed מצורע, who is MORE impure, is permitted, while the healed man who is counting is forbidden. That is exactly רבי יהודה's view, and the next step argues with it.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
"Seven days they shall count for him"
the days of his counting, and not the days of his confirmed state.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים יִסְפְּרוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא; this is the opinion that supports the 'yes'.
steps.raayaObject: That a מוחלט is permitted in marital relations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה in the ברייתא: forbidden in counting days, not in confirmed days.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: all the more so in the confirmed days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argues with a קל וחומר that if the counting days are forbidden, the confirmed days are surely forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: if the seven counting days are forbidden, then by a קל וחומר, the confirmed days are forbidden too.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings a disagreeing opinion. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a confirmed מצורע is also forbidden to his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: the counting days are a lighter state of impurity than the confirmed days. If even the lighter state forbids him, the heavier state must forbid him all the more. So according to him, the answer to step 8 would be 'no'.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a stricter one: if the light case has the rule, the strict case surely does

phrases.english: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says:
The seven days of his counting are forbidden,
so all the more so the days of his confirmed state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion in the same ברייתא, against רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A confirmed מצורע is forbidden to his wife, by קל וחומר from the counting days.

steps.title: רבי חייא and רבי: King עוזיהו had יותם while a confirmed מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא points to King עוזיהו, whose son יותם was born while he was a confirmed מצורע, and רבי agrees that a מוחלט is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said: I discussed this before רבי. I said: You taught us that עוזיהו had his son יותם only during the days when he was a confirmed מצורע. רבי answered: I also said so.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a proof for the lenient view from a story in תנ"ך. רבי agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יותם was born while עוזיהו was a confirmed מצורע, then עוזיהו was with his wife during that time. This shows a מוחלט is permitted, against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רבי's reply 'I also said so' confirms he holds the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: I discussed / argued the matter in front of
A king of יהודה who was struck with צרעת
I too said so

phrases.english: And רבי חייא said,
I discussed this before רבי:
You taught us, our teacher,
that עוזיהו did not have יותם
except during the days of his confirmed state,
phrases.notes: So עוזיהו was with his wife while a confirmed מצורע, which means it is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אֲנִי כָּךְ אָמַרְתִּי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I too said so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא, דַּנְתִּי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's lenient view against the קל וחומר of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a מוחלט is permitted to his wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The tradition that יותם was born to עוזיהו while he was a confirmed מצורע; רבי agrees.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step. It asks for the underlying reason behind the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions read the same פסוק about the counting days. The question is why one stretches it to the confirmed days and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to explain the dispute of steps 10–11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute.

steps.title: Stretch the Torah's rule, or keep to what it wrote
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that what the Torah wrote for the counting days applies all the more to the confirmed days; the other view holds we apply only what the Torah actually wrote.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds: the Torah revealed the prohibition for the counting days, so all the more it applies to the confirmed days. The other Sage holds: what the Torah revealed, it revealed; what it did not reveal, it did not reveal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the core of the argument. It is about whether to add to a Torah prohibition by logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses a 'כל שכן': the Torah gave the example of the lighter state, and the heavier state is included automatically. The other Sage says the Torah chose to forbid only the counting days, so we do not extend it. That is why a מוחלט is permitted in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') revealed
All the more so
What it revealed, it revealed (only that)
The other Sage (here, רבי יהודה)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה (and רבי), a מוחלט is permitted to his wife and only the counting days are forbidden, because we apply only what the Torah wrote. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids both by קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the assumption from step 7: a מוחלט may be with his wife, so purifying him would actually start a time when he is forbidden to her.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה holds:
The Torah revealed it for the days of his counting,
and all the more so for the days of his confirmed state.
And the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This means רבי יהודה, from step 10.

phrases.english: What it revealed, it revealed,
and what it did not reveal, it did not reveal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּימֵי סְפִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether to extend the Torah's prohibition by כל שכן, or to keep it only to the counting days the Torah mentioned.

steps.title: Does the matter really depend on the priest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the status of a נגע truly depends on the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that the whole matter depends on the priest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier idea on the daf and asks a clarifying question: does it really depend on the כהן whether a person becomes טמא from a נגע? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נגע does not make someone טמא by itself. The כהן has to look at it and declare it. The גמרא wants to confirm that this means the כהן can also choose when to look, or hold off.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? A question that checks what follows from an idea
The matter depends (on)
Priest. Only he can declare a נגע טמא or טהור

phrases.english: Is this to say that the matter depends on the priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the מצורע discussion back to the earlier topic of the כהן's role in examining נגעים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether declaring a נגע, and the timing of the examination, depends on the כהן.

steps.title: Yes: a ברייתא learns from 'on the day it appears'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק as saying there are days the כהן does not look.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, and so it is taught: 'And on the day it appears in him.' There is a day when you look at it, and there is a day when you do not look at it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'yes' and supports this with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on the day' look extra. They teach that only certain days are days for examining. So on some days the כהן does not look at the נגע at all, which proves that the כהן controls the timing.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
And on the day it appears in him (the פסוק being read)

phrases.english: Yes, and so it is taught:
"And on the day it appears in him."
There is a day on which you examine him,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ יוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה רוֹאֶה בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and there is a day on which you do not examine him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That the timing of the examination depends on the כהן.

steps.title: A groom and a festival get seven days before the examination
steps.stepSummary: From that reading, רבי יהודה rules that a חתן gets his seven feast days and anyone gets the seven days of the רגל before the כהן looks.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: a groom on whom a נגע appeared is given the seven days of the wedding feast. This applies to him, his house, and his clothing. The same is true on a festival: he is given the seven days of the festival. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives practical rules that come from 'there is a day you do not look.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are days the כהן does not look, he waits during a חתן's seven days of celebration and during the seven days of a רגל, so the person's joy is not spoiled. This covers a נגע on the body, on the house, or on clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Groom
The seven days of the wedding feast
A צרעת mark (on a person, house, or garment)
A pilgrimage festival

phrases.english: From here they said:
A groom on whom a נגע appeared,
we give him the seven days of the wedding feast.
For him, for his house, and for his clothing.
And similarly on a festival:
we give him the seven days of the festival,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading from step 16 to practical cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The examination of a נגע waits during a חתן's seven feast days and during the seven days of a רגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule behind holding off on examining נגעים during celebrations, which connects to the topic of חול המועד in this מסכת.

steps.title: רבי learns the same rule from emptying the house
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the reading is not needed. If the כהן waits so the owners can empty a house, which is only optional, he surely waits for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: it is not needed. The Torah says: 'And the priest shall command, and they shall empty the house.' If we wait for him for an optional matter, all the more so for a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי agrees with the rule, but he offers a different source for it: a קל וחומר from a נגע on a house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah tells the כהן to wait while the owners take their things out of the house, so the things will not become טמא. Saving one's belongings is only a דבר הרשות, something optional. If the כהן waits for that, he surely waits for a דבר מצוה like a חתן's joy or the joy of a רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (that proof is unnecessary)
And they shall empty the house
An optional matter, not a מצוה
All the more so

phrases.english: רבי says: it is not needed.
phrases.notes: He agrees with the rule. He just says you don't need the words 'on the day' to prove it.

phrases.english: For it says:
"And the priest shall command, and they shall empty the house."
If we wait for him for an optional matter,
all the more so for a matter of מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with רבי יהודה's ruling but gives a different source for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiting for a מצוה is learned through a קל וחומר from waiting to empty a house, which is only optional.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not arguing with the rule itself. Both agree the כהן waits for a חתן and for a רגל. The argument here is only about where the rule comes from.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there is any real difference between רבי יהודה and רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: Both views reach the same rule, so the גמרא asks whether anything changes depending on which source you use. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both say the כהן waits for a חתן and a רגל, the dispute could be only about sources. The גמרא wants to know if the two views lead to any different ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what separates the two sources given in steps 17 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a practical difference between רבי יהודה and רבי.

steps.title: אביי: they differ only in how they read the verses
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference is only in how each one reads the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the difference between them is the meaning they read into the verses.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the two views have no practical difference. They only read the פסוקים differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the ruling comes out the same either way. Each תנא simply reads the other's פסוק differently, so the argument is only about learning the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: The meaning they read into the verses
There is (a difference) between them

phrases.english: אביי said:
The meaning they read into the verses is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַשְׁמָעוּת דּוֹרְשִׁין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No practical difference; only how the פסוקים are read.

steps.title: רבא: they differ about waiting for an optional matter
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is a practical difference: whether the examination waits for a דבר הרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: an optional matter is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He says the two views lead to a different ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's source is the house case, where the כהן waits even for something optional. So he would also wait for a דבר הרשות. רבי יהודה's source teaches only about days of מצוה, such as a חתן and a רגל, so for him the כהן waits only for a מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees the כהן waits for a חתן's seven days and the seven days of a רגל. אביי says רבי יהודה and רבי differ only in how they read the פסוקים. רבא says they differ in practice: whether the כהן also waits for something optional.

phrases.english: And רבא said:
An optional matter is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means: does the כהן also wait for something that is not a מצוה? רבי's house case suggests he does.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 19 that disagrees with אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A practical difference: whether the examination is delayed for an optional matter. רבי says yes, and רבי יהודה says only for a מצוה.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה learn from the house case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה does not learn from נגעי בתים that the examination waits even for an optional reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? Why doesn't he learn from the house case that the כהן waits even for an optional reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רבי יהודה's view. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a house, the כהן waits so the owners can take their things out, and that is only a דבר הרשות. So why doesn't רבי יהודה say the same for a person's body or clothing? The two words 'and רבי יהודה' stand for this whole question.

keyTerms.meaning: An optional matter, not a מצוה
Signs of צרעת on a house
Emptying the house before the כהן looks

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה?
phrases.notes: The full question is: why doesn't רבי יהודה learn from the house, where the כהן waits for an optional reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רבי יהודה's side of the practical difference רבא described in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה does not allow the examination to wait for a דבר הרשות, when the house case shows waiting for an optional reason

steps.title: The house case is a one-of-a-kind rule
steps.stepSummary: We do not learn from נגעי בתים, because that law is a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not learn from there, because it is a חידוש, a one-of-a-kind rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה does not learn from the house case, because the laws of צרעת on a house are unusual and stand alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה gives an unusual rule, we keep it inside its own case and do not spread it to other cases. Waiting for an optional reason stays limited to houses. For a person or clothing, רבי יהודה only lets the examination wait for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: From there
We do not learn or derive
A one-of-a-kind law that does not follow the usual pattern

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה lets the examination wait only for a מצוה. The waiting in the house case is a חידוש, so we do not learn other cases from it.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the house is outside the laws of צרעת. נגעי בתים is fully a kind of צרעת. Only this special rule about waiting stays limited to houses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a rule that comes up all over ש"ס: a חידוש stays within its own case and is not used to learn other laws.

phrases.english: From there we do not learn,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the house case, where the כהן waits so the owners can empty the house.

phrases.english: because it is a novelty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נגעי בתים is a חידוש, so we do not learn from it that other examinations wait for a דבר הרשות
